diagnostic.q: Have you seen fish or repeated feeding signs within range?
diagnostic.no: Before changing bait, observe the water, margins, bays and edges. Consider moving.
diagnostic.unknown: Watch dawn, dusk and quiet periods; one bubble is insufficient.
diagnostic.yes: Fish are nearby. Check presentation before changing flavour.

diagnostic.q: After checking, are you confident the hook and hooklink lie cleanly?
diagnostic.no: Retrieve, check weed and silt, adjust length or presentation, or find a clear opening.
diagnostic.unknown: Retrieve one rig and inspect lead, hook and material on the hooklink.
diagnostic.yes: Presentation looks plausible. Check depth and firmness.

diagnostic.q: Have you confirmed bottom and depth with a repeat scan or a lead?
diagnostic.no: Check the edge, weed height and how far the lead sinks. Choose a safe landing route.
diagnostic.unknown: Repeat the scan track and compare lead contact at the same distance.
diagnostic.yes: The spot is better understood. Check whether conditions have changed.

diagnostic.q: Are weather, wind and water temperature similar to the start of the session?
diagnostic.no: Update your working idea: compare oxygenated areas, depths and banks affected by wind.
diagnostic.unknown: Record the water and wind trend; do not infer feeding from pressure alone.
diagnostic.yes: Conditions are stable. Assess the food amount.

diagnostic.q: Does the food amount match activity and the number of fish?
diagnostic.no: If you may have overfed, stop topping up and try one hookbait nearby. If fish are clearly feeding, add food gradually.
diagnostic.unknown: Check whether food disappears; other species may be consuming it.
diagnostic.yes: The amount seems reasonable. Only now compare hookbaits.

diagnostic.q: Have you tested one bait or colour contrast without changing everything else?
diagnostic.no: Compare a natural wafter with a visible pop-up or topper, or change hookbait size. Keep other variables stable.
diagnostic.unknown: Record what is on each rig and change one thing.
diagnostic.yes: After a fair comparison, consider the rig or a neighbouring spot.

diagnostic.q: Is the current rig safe and suited to bottom and weed?
diagnostic.no: Check the Rigs section, safe lead release and presentation. Do not tie a complex rig blindly.
diagnostic.unknown: Inspect the settled rig and its safety after a break before recasting.
diagnostic.yes: The rig looks suitable. Give the spot time or test another depth.

diagnostic.q: After enough observation, are there still signs of fish at this spot?
diagnostic.no: Move one rig to another side of the feature, another depth or a quieter route.
diagnostic.unknown: Set an observation window and Plan B rather than recasting constantly.
diagnostic.yes: Give the area time, limit disturbance and record what changed.

cold.title: <8°C
cold.bait: small, easy-to-check wafter or neutral bottom bait
cold.flavour: a bait that releases attractants in cold water, perhaps a sweet or moderate fishmeal profile; check ingredients and oils
cold.feed: small PVA bag or a few baits; no top-up without feeding signs
cold.backup: If quiet, locate fish at another depth before changing flavour.

cool.title: 8–16°C
cool.bait: bottom bait or wafter on verified ground; pop-up above sediment
cool.flavour: fishmeal with garlic or a subtle cream/fruit contrast
cool.feed: small starting amount, increased only after a response
cool.backup: Compare a warming spot with adjacent deeper water.

warm.title: 16–24°C
warm.bait: bottom bait or wafter, optionally a bright topper as one test
warm.flavour: fishmeal, krill/spice or fruit contrast as a comparison
warm.feed: adjust to feeding carp and other fish
warm.backup: If fish are not feeding, check cover and oxygen rather than adding more food.

hot.title: >24°C
hot.bait: small hookbait that is easy to check
hot.flavour: no flavour replaces oxygen and location
hot.feed: feed cautiously and put fish welfare first
hot.backup: If oxygen is poor, stop fishing or choose a safer area.

hard.presentation: bottom bait or wafter on clear bottom
hard.rig: short to medium hooklink; verify a safe lead clip
hard.length: try about 15–25 cm initially, then verify how the rig lands
hard.feed: small concentrated or lightly scattered portion

silt.presentation: wafter or low pop-up above sediment
silt.rig: safe lead release, lighter lead and hooklink not dragged into silt
silt.length: determine after measuring sinking depth; often longer than on firm bottom
silt.feed: small verified patch; avoid burying fine feed

weed.presentation: pop-up or wafter above low weed, or bottom bait in a clear hole
weed.rig: safe landing route and lead release
weed.length: match actual weed height and size of the clear patch
weed.feed: precisely into an opening or on a clean edge

transition.presentation: compare a bottom bait on the firm side with a wafter on the soft side
transition.rig: first confirm which side the lead actually reaches
transition.length: according to sediment and how the rig lands
transition.feed: small amounts on both sides as a controlled comparison

pressure.high: Reduce noise and recasting; try a single or natural hookbait on a quieter side.
pressure.low: You can compare a wider area, but do not automatically feed heavily.

visibility.clear: Compare natural or washed-out with one visible contrast.
visibility.murky: First put the bait near fish; white, yellow or scent is a test, not a guarantee.

activity.seen: Place a safe rig near confirmed signs and reduce disturbance.
activity.not-seen: Observe and scan first; bait recommendations have low confidence.

season.winter: A winter label does not replace measuring water temperature.
season.spring: Compare warming areas and cooler water.
season.spawning: Do not target spawning fish; follow local restrictions.
season.summer: Watch oxygen and fish welfare in heat.
season.autumn: Check the trend over several days, not just the month.

weather.stable: Give a confirmed spot enough time in stable weather.
weather.changing: When a front changes, watch fish and reconsider depth; do not rely on hPa alone.

wind.toward: Check the windward bank, considering temperature and safety.
wind.away: Compare the sheltered side and inflows; avoid a universal wind-direction rule.

depth.shallow: Shallows can warm or lose oxygen quickly; compare nearby deep water.
depth.deep: Deep water guarantees neither fish nor oxygen; check water layers.

plateau: A: clean top if fish are active and the rig lands properly
B: side or upper edge along a fish route
C: less-fished base or bottom transition
slope: B: base of the drop if silt is not too deep
C: side shelf away from the main boat track
trench: A: channel entrance or firmer side
B: channel bottom after checking oxygen and sediment
weed: C: quieter corridor or inner edge
transition: B: soft side with the hookbait above sediment
C: adjacent, less-fished part of the transition

scanChecklist: Lead or marker confirmation where safe and permitted
